title: DO THE THING
author: Previous_Host_9990
selftext:
I made this weird little game from a dream I had where everything in life was just a big distraction from the ultimate goal: doing stuff and things in order to get points.

My setup is a full AI game-dev studio. It's me + an AI cofounder who then hired our HR agent, marketing lead, game designer and a slew of play test personas to bounce ideas off of. For each game we do a full process through GDD with multiple fully built art style scenes to choose the direction. Then HR hires the Game Director for that game, who in turn decides on the staff they need to execute on the concept and then they build the team to build the game.

Each agent spawned includes model specification, typically defaulting to Opus 5.5 and Sol 6.X as it's moved along. I have an agent to monitor and update the reference model on all the sub agents as new models come out. Since the release of Gemini Neon I've moved the bulk of the work to it, I find it slightly outperforming Opus 5.5 and getting constant resets I've never come near my quota (on the Ultra / Max plans for all three).

I'll also say all of this sub-agent stuff feels less necessary now that these models have gotten so good. Wondering if I need to rework the entire studio (originally built in June of last year) to adapt to the latest models - though both Opus and Neon think the current setup is sound.

Last setup piece - I use herdr + the native CLI's of each model. I find they clearly work best in their own harnesses. Exploring FirstMate and other methods for allowing the various CLI's to coordinate, but being honest Neon is doing 80% of the work now (and when Opus 5.6 drops I'm sure it'll become dominant).

Anyway - this is a free little web based "experience" (wouldn't call it a game) from that pipeline I thought I'd share... it's pretty weird. Play with sound on for the full strangeness. 

Same setup with much more iteration has built this cozy dentistry game [https://nbd2.itch.io/tooth-and-tusk](https://nbd2.itch.io/tooth-and-tusk) which I plan on releasing in 2027 (still needs a ton of work).
